clue.text: Arms possibly fifty-one medical men

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one
MBs are Bachelors of Medicine, i.e. doctors

explanation.surface: Fifty-one doctors are lined up, perhaps carrying weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' suggests weapons, but it means the upper limbs; 'possibly' marks it as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are examples of the body's jointed appendages, legs being the others.

clue.text: Taking direction on appointment, appears unflappable

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a compass direction
a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: Someone told where to go for their appointment looks perfectly calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate describes a calm, composed manner that nothing ruffles.

clue.text: Declare a man in it to be in error

indicators.note: something in error is wrong, so these letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a certain man must be mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' shuffles A MAN IN IT; 'to be' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to assert or declare it firmly.

clue.text: Obligatory wrapping

definitions.meaning: a contract that must be honoured is legally compulsory
a book's cover, or a strip of material wound around something

explanation.definitionFit: A compulsory agreement is binding, and binding is also tape or material wound round an object.

clue.text: Being malign, this is left

definitions.meaning: in heraldry, the left-hand side of a shield as borne

explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means threatening evil, and in heraldry it denotes the left side, from the Latin word for left.

clue.text: House in ruins-dire scene!

indicators.note: something in ruins is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A home has been wrecked, and the sight is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ruins' rearranges DIRE SCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a dwelling place, the home where someone lives.

clue.text: Many in time look back-such a bloomer!

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: turning back means the word for look is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: Many people, looking back, regret such a blunder in their time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AIR into RIA. 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The cineraria is a flowering garden plant, so it is literally something that blooms.

clue.text: What's put inside a sea-going vessel

definitions.meaning: a lining, such as a bin bag or a coat lining, fitted inside something
a large passenger ship on a regular route

explanation.definitionFit: A liner is an inner lining fitted inside something, and also an ocean-going passenger ship.

clue.text: Caught and bolted a quantity of fish

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to bolt is to run away, so bolted gives ran

explanation.surface: A caught fish that got away from the angler.
explanation.walkthrough: A cran is a Scottish measure of fresh herrings, about 37.5 gallons.
explanation.definitionFit: A cran is a measure used for landed herrings, so it names an amount of catch.

clue.text: Got to bed in a break

indicators.note: to break something is to smash it, so these letters are shattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone managed to get to bed during a short rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges TO BED IN A; 'break' reads as a holiday but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtained is a synonym of acquired or got.

clue.text: Right and wrong about top grade fruit

indicators.note: the letters for right and wrong are placed around the top grade, splitting them

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
A1 is the top grade, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A moral debate about which fruit is first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts AI between R and SIN. A1 (top quality, from Lloyd's ship grading) is read as the letters AI.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a common dried fruit.

clue.text: Turn in goal and even nearly score

indicators.note: to turn something round is to reverse it, so the following little word is read backwards

parts.note: the net is the goal in football
e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: A footballer turns in the goalmouth and nearly evens the score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reverses IN to NI. A score is twenty, so one short of it is nearly a score.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, and one fewer than twenty is almost a score.

clue.text: Roll in, opening with a duck and ending weary

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letters, here taken from weary

explanation.surface: A tired cricketer rolls in after opening the batting and scoring nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes RY, the close of WEARY. A duck is a cricket score of zero, looking like O.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll is a list of names or items, and an inventory is a detailed list of goods.

clue.text: There's little time for pressing

definitions.meaning: a moment or very short interval

explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a moment, and as an adjective it means urgent or immediate.

clue.text: Politicians accepting a guy's explanations

indicators.note: the politicians take the man inside themselves, so his letters go into the middle of theirs

parts.note: Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party
a guy is a man, he

explanation.surface: Conservative MPs take on board some fellow's account of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts HE inside TORIES. Tories are Britain's Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Theories are proposed accounts that explain why something happens.

clue.text: Withdraw brochure after centre-spread

indicators.note: the pamphlet comes after the middle letters in the answer
the centre of a word is its middle letters, here those of spread

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet or leaflet

explanation.surface: Pull the brochure after it appears in the magazine's centre-spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes RE, the two middle letters of SPREAD; 'centre-spread' looks like a magazine's middle pages.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to take back or withdraw a statement or a part.

clue.text: There's intense discord about one eminent scientist

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed around the numeral for one
discord is disagreement or jangling, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Fierce disagreement surrounds a famous scientist's ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discord' rearranges INTENSE and 'about' puts it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein, the physicist behind relativity, is the most famous of all scientists.

clue.text: Children holding a churchman up will get parted

indicators.note: the children's word holds the churchman inside it

parts.note: seed means offspring, as in biblical usage

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman

explanation.surface: Children taking a vicar on their shoulders will be separated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses REV to VER (a down-clue convention) and 'holding' puts it inside SEED; 'will get' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Severed means cut apart or separated, a synonym of parted.

clue.text: When properly prepared, eat 27 across produce

indicators.note: preparing something properly means arranging it into a new form, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the answer to 27 across is green

explanation.surface: Eat your greens when cooked properly, and grow your own produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When properly prepared' rearranges EAT plus GREEN, the answer to 27 across. 'produce' looks like a noun, vegetables, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to bring something into being, i.e. to produce it.

clue.text: Colourless article written before retiring

indicators.note: the article is written before the word for retiring in the answer

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
retiring means shy or reserved

explanation.surface: A dull piece of writing, published before someone retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' suggests leaving work but means shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means pale as ashes, drained of colour.

clue.text: No good place of seclusion

parts.note: OK means all right, i.e. good

explanation.surface: A secluded spot that is not much good.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a sheltered corner or recess where one can be alone.

clue.text: In the ambassador a clerk found a fount of wisdom

indicators.note: the answer sits in these words, its letters running across the word gap

explanation.surface: A clerk at the embassy proves to be a source of great wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' and 'found' frame the run; it spans ambassadOR A CLErk.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle was a priest or shrine giving divine counsel, hence any source of wise advice.

clue.text: Keep quiet about much inertia

indicators.note: the call for quiet goes around the word for much

parts.note: sh is the call to keep quiet
a lot means much

explanation.surface: Saying nothing about it is a sign of real laziness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts LOT inside SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is laziness, a reluctance to move or work.

clue.text: Stiffening agent finding a way to bow

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
an arch is a bow or curved shape

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a method of making a bow stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' suggests archery but means a curve, an arch.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is used to stiffen collars and fabrics.

clue.text: New colour

explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or new to something, and it is also the colour of grass.

clue.text: Decree support is overdue

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
late means overdue

explanation.surface: A ruling that support payments are overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decree' looks like a noun but is the verb.
